gen-dafont-origami-gf-heebo: Heebo reads tall and tidy, with curves that stop short of closing. Origami's brush-pen strokes never vary in pressure, and that stubborn constant line against the sans-serif text is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-hind-guntur: Origami lays down single-stroke brush letters with a lowercase as dense as poured lead type. Hind Guntur, a sans-serif, stays lean and stamped-looking, with wide gaps where its curves meet the stems.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-hind-madurai: Approachable, first of all, thanks to Hind Madurai. Its sans-serif lowercase fills the line like capitals, and its s curves open wide, while Origami carries the loud, brushed single-stroke personality on top.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-hind-mysuru: Hind Mysuru reads contemporary and crisp, its lowercase pressing up near the ascenders. Origami's heavy brush strokes get the display role, so a modest body size under them lets the sans-serif text stay quiet.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-hind-siliguri: Hind Siliguri hums along in a flat gray of constant line weight, rounds slightly cracked open. Origami is the loud one, a brush-stroke display face, while the sans keeps quiet.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-hind-vadodara: Origami comes in like a sign painter's single brush stroke. It is best at bold, quirky display, while Hind Vadodara's tall bowls and spacious terminal gaps keep the sans text open.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-huninn: Huninn rises close to cap height, with crossbars as fat as their stems. And Origami's poured-lead lowercase can go large above it, while the sans text below stays modest.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight bends its lines like tubing, with short ascenders and curve tails held back from the body. But Origami's brush-painted lowercase gives the sans a strong, unmistakable partner in weight and personality.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-karla: Karla's gaping c and tall middle band make its lines look stocky and friendly beside the heading. Origami does the curvy brush work; the sans does the plain talking.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-kedebideri: Approachable is the mood here, with Kedebideri's rounded letters staying open under a skyward x-height. Origami lays its rope-like single strokes into display shapes, while Kedebideri handles the plain sans text.
